TERRA-G01.title: Transitive preflight and atomic commit protocol

preflight_dependency_checks.evidence: PrimitiveExecutor.execute performs no dependency walk; it resolves one primitive and calls it. SemanticExecutor._execute_operations walks operations sequentially and discovers an unsupported operation at the moment it reaches it (reference_execution.py L526-L539, _execute_operation L590-L657).

structured_rejection.evidence: battle_sandbox/errors.py typed hierarchy + semantic_provenance_ref in trace; game_data raises SemanticExecutionError with operation_id-prefixed messages and behavior_compiler produces named diagnostics (EXECUTABLE_REFERENCE_* reason codes).
structured_rejection.gap: No rejection object carrying affected state families / evidence request / pending obligations; diagnostics never reach the sandbox API because step() is a stub.

transaction_or_staged_delta.evidence: No staging buffer, no private delta, no transaction-owned RNG object anywhere in src/.

atomic_state_commit.evidence: battle_runtime primitives write directly into BattleState and ExecutionContext.trace (e.g. turns.py::advance_to_next_actor mutates state.turn_timeline in place; property/hp primitives write lists into state dicts).

state_revision.evidence: No revision field, no staleness check.

evidence: game_data/reference_execution.py::SandboxRng.draw_01 RETURNS a new frozen rng value instead of mutating, so a rejected reference fold leaks no RNG advance
battle_sandbox.rng.SandboxRng IS mutable and public (randint/uniform/next_u64) - a rejected primitive that drew before raising would leak a draw

allocator_no_consume_on_rejection.evidence: battle_runtime/modifiers.py::_next_instance_ordinal is computed from current list contents just before the write, so a mid-flight failure after one target was appended leaves that target's container already written (see the per-target loop in reference_execution._execute_add_modifier L1199-L1225 and battle_runtime._modifier_state_write_impl).

queue_no_mutation_on_rejection.evidence: PendingInsertedAction append enforces enqueue_index == current pending queue length and returns a new state (reference_execution.py L319-L322); battle_sandbox has no queue.

dependency_closure.evidence: The closest behaviour is behavior_compiler's whole-record 'structural_only' flag: if any node binds to STRUCTURAL_CALL_ONLY / STRUCTURAL_PACKET_ONLY, the entire behavior becomes non-executable. That is a coarse global deny, not a per-action reachable-closure certificate.

production_conflict_paths.why: The live ExecutionContext (and therefore BattleState) is handed straight to the implementation. There is no staging object, so any raise inside the implementation occurs after writes already applied.

Property primitives attach a boundary sink that records PropertyChangeBoundary events into the live trace as mutations are accepted; a later rejection leaves accepted boundary events in the branch trace.

Mutates state.turn_timeline in place and rewrites property 38 for every participant in a loop; UnsupportedTurnParticipantError / TurnSemanticError raised on any later participant leaves earlier participants already recharged. It also raises TurnCompletionRequiredError only after the phase read, and _delay_entry can raise inside the sort.

Iterates resolved targets and commits per-target modifier state; a failure on target N returns only after targets 1..N-1 were folded, and the reference model has no rollback (reference-model scope only).
Runs one child TaskList per selected target; a rejection in a later child leaves the earlier child effects folded into the private state.

non_conflicts: reference_execution._execute_operations returns state only on success, so callers of SemanticExecutor observe no partial state (but also no partial-effect diagnostics and no rejection certificate).
Reference-layer dataclasses are frozen and every transition uses dataclasses.replace, so aliasing is not a mutation hazard.
battle_sandbox.state.BattleState.__post_init__ deep-copies all inputs, so caller-owned containers never alias kernel state.

EXISTS_CONFLICTING: incremental mutation before unsupported-operation discovery (see production_conflict_paths)

risks.detail: F02 must reshape the single state container consumed by ~90 registered primitives plus five reference modules. The executor hands the live context to implementations (LSD-01), so there is no seam to migrate behind.

risks.risk: Two incompatible RNG ownership models already coexist
risks.detail: Reference-layer RNG is a frozen value with no leak on rejection; sandbox RNG is a mutable public object. Choosing one silently determines whether G01's 'identical RNG state and draw count on rejection' test can pass.

risks.risk: A registered production primitive implements one explicitly superseded rule
risks.detail: FC-02: battle_runtime.modifiers._apply_redd_life_core groups REFRESH with REPLACE and writes count. The freeze wins and the audit does not repair it, so the conflict stays live until Terra touches modifier lifecycle.

tests/battle_ir is already failing (3 stale catalog count assertions) and full-suite discovery raises ImportError because tests/ is not a package. Terra cannot rely on a red/green signal until both are addressed.

astra_semantic_freeze_v1.json, astra_reverse_master_v1.json and the 2026-09-20 handoff exist only in the working tree. Any clean checkout or migration loses the authority this audit was performed against.

The strings 'EXECUTABLE_REFERENCE' (compile_status), 'executable' (boolean), 'EXACT_CONFIG_ID' and 'golden_eligible' all read as stronger than their scope. The freeze explicitly warns a compiler flag is insufficient.

risks.risk: Reference-model conveniences are reachable from production paths
risks.detail: behavior_compiler gates RETARGET to ModifierOwnerAdjoinEntity and the reference executor consumes target_semantics_reference._adjoin (position arithmetic + entity_id tie break). A future alias being added to that allowlist would promote the quarantined convenience.

risks.risk: Ordering helper shared across incompatible purposes
risks.detail: hash.stable_json_hash sorts every mapping recursively. Using it while building descriptors would satisfy the letter of canonical serialization while creating the exact order-from-keys failure the freeze forbids.

risks.risk: Silent absence loss at the state boundary
risks.detail: BattleState.from_dict defaults every absent store to {} (FC-19). Once F01 introduces presence, every existing from_dict path becomes a lossy migration and needs an explicit decision per store.

risks.risk: Scenario wave flattening leaks into descriptors
risks.detail: scenario_compiler already flattens groups and sorts by wave_index; if R01 reuses ScenarioPackage as its scenario descriptor, the freeze's SOURCE_ORDER_ONLY wave contract is violated at birth.

risks.risk: Monster AI has no representation surface at all
risks.detail: R01 must create AI policy/state descriptors from scratch while D5 records native admission, precedence, DefaultDSE and commit as unknown. The descriptor must therefore be purely representational; nothing in the repo helps police that boundary.

risks.risk: Local dependencies not in the Astra graph
risks.detail: Twelve local software dependencies (LSD-01..LSD-12) sit outside the Astra F01->{F02,R01}->G01 graph. A planner that respects only the semantic graph will be surprised by LSD-01/LSD-09/LSD-10 on the first commit.

planner_inputs: Freeze-derived dependency order F01 -> {F02, R01} -> G01 is confirmed as the correct *semantic* order and is respected by this audit. No Astra graph change is proposed.
F01 is the only ticket with zero blocked dependencies and it is the only place where the presence and identity vocabulary can be introduced before the state container is reshaped. Start there.

F01 must land the presence envelope BEFORE F02's snapshot/hash, because BattleState.from_dict, SandboxSnapshot and stable_json_hash form a single serialization contract (LSD-03) and hash.stable_json_hash also silently coerces tuples (FC-19).

F02's hardest decision is not the schema, it is the migration seam: executor.py hands the live ExecutionContext to ~90 registered primitives (LSD-01). Decide explicitly whether F02 keeps a compatibility adapter over the JSON store or freezes battle_runtime first.
Adopt exactly one RNG ownership model before G01 (LSD-05 / RK-02). The reference-layer frozen-value pattern is the one that already satisfies 'rejection leaves RNG unchanged'.
G01's preflight must not be built on behavior_compiler's coarse structural_only flag; that is a whole-record deny, not a reachable-closure certificate.
G01's acceptance tests are already written verbatim in terra_roadmap[3].tests and step_transaction_contract.acceptance_tests; use them as the ticket's definition of done without rewording.

R01 must produce descriptors that preserve [] vs [null], source group/slot identity and repeated occurrences; do not reuse ScenarioCompiler waves (RK-10) and do not reuse resolve_target_alias's flat id tuple as the lostless target descriptor.

Before R01, decide the fate of the three reachable reference conveniences (FC-04 target adjacency + entity_id ties, FC-02/FC-03 modifier Refresh, FC-07 scenario wave sort). The cheapest safe option is an explicit quarantine boundary plus a test that the production path cannot reach them.

Treat the following as authorized prerequisites that are NOT semantic work: (a) tests/__init__.py so the documented suite command runs, (b) repointing the three catalog count assertions in tests/battle_ir/test_semantic_batch_catalog.py to a derived count, (c) committing the untracked Astra authority artifacts.
Do not classify any unresolved native semantic question as work for a cheap model. Software-difficulty classification is provided only for implementation complexity (cheap_model_suitability).
